name: Chaff
author: E. T. Carter
description: A lush field of grass fills the lower frame in receding depth ranks, leaning strokes combed downwind as travelling gust fronts ripple across and light their tips. Each front shakes a drift of glowing chaff motes loose from the grass that lift, stream downwind on shallow ballistic arcs, tumble and fade — dust blowing through the field rather than floating on black. Every mote's position is a pure function of the shared gust schedule and a per-mote hash, so the field is stateless and seamlessly looping; motes blend their hue through all four palette colours.

params.label: Gust rate
params.effect: How often a gust front combs the grass and shakes loose a new drift of chaff; low leaves long calms, high keeps the air busy with overlapping releases.

params.label: Grass density
params.effect: How thickly the grass blades pack the field, from a sparse stand to a dense lush meadow.

params.label: Grass height
params.effect: Height of the grass blades, from low turf to tall waving stalks filling the frame.

params.label: Chaff density
params.effect: Hash-gated fraction of candidate motes that actually release per gust, thinning the dust to a few flecks or filling the air with a thick shed.

params.label: Drift
params.effect: How far downwind and how high the motes are carried before they decelerate and fade; low gives short tumbling hops, high streams them across the field.

params.label: Mote size
params.effect: CSS-pixel size of each chaff fleck, from fine drifting dust to coarse confetti.
